answer: A concrete sybil defense is bonded admission: each agent locks a stake before joining, and a validation kernel issues every new identity a fresh puzzle derived from recent ledger activity. Honest agents echo back a signed proof on time, and voting weight follows stake plus verified uptime. During an attack, trust sinks to its nadir, so slashing activates: wrong or duplicated answers burn the bond. Each fake identity then costs locked capital plus computation that cannot be reused, making cheap bot floods unprofitable.
